entries.headline: DoorDash offers $65 a share, valuing Instacart at about $17 billion
entries.dek: The cash-and-stock bid is a 26% premium to Instacart's October 22 closing price, with the deal targeted to close by the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028.
entries.caption: A grocery delivery bag sits on an empty loading dock at dusk, crates of produce stacked nearby.
unverified_claims: DoorDash's projection of more than $500 million in annual synergies within several years of closing is the company's own estimate.
The expected closing timeline of late 2027 or the first half of 2028 is the companies' own target and subject to change.
brief: DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart, operated by Maplebear Inc., in a deal valuing the grocery-delivery company at about $17 billion. Instacart shareholders can choose $65.00 in cash per share, 0.3372 of a DoorDash share, or a mix of $48.75 cash plus 0.0843 of a DoorDash share for each share they hold.

Instacart's board approved the deal unanimously, and holders of about 19% of its shares have agreed to vote for it. DoorDash will fund the cash portion from cash on hand and debt, including a 364-day bridge loan from JPMorgan Chase, with closing targeted for the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and antitrust approval.

On the venture boards, the agriculture and food theme comprises 16 listed names; seven traded today, two higher and two lower, for a median move of +0.00% against -1.47% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. No name traded enough volume to clear the board's liquidity floor, so none is named here.
body: DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart, which operates under the legal name Maplebear Inc., in a deal that values the grocery-delivery company at approximately $17 billion. Instacart shareholders will be able to elect one of three forms of consideration for each share held: $65.00 in cash, 0.3372 of a DoorDash share, or a combination of $48.75 in cash and 0.0843 of a DoorDash share. The stock portion of the total consideration is capped at 25% of the deal's aggregate value, with proration mechanics built in should stock elections be oversubscribed.

The per-share price represents a 26% premium to Instacart's closing stock price on October 22, 2026, according to the companies' release. Instacart's board of directors unanimously approved the transaction, and shareholders holding approximately 19% of the company's outstanding shares have already agreed to vote in favour of the deal.

DoorDash said it intends to fund the cash portion of the deal using cash on hand together with proceeds from new debt, and has arranged a 364-day bridge loan facility from JPMorgan Chase. The company said the transaction carries no financing condition and that it is targeting investment-grade credit ratings. DoorDash said the combination is expected to generate more than $500 million in annual synergies within several years of closing.

Completion is expected by the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028. The deal still requires Instacart shareholder approval, clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust act in the United States, and regulatory approvals in Canada and Israel, along with other customary closing conditions.

On the venture boards, the agriculture and food theme comprises 16 listed venture names. Seven traded today, two higher and two lower, for a median move of +0.00% against a decline of -1.47% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 1.47 percentage points on the day.

None of the theme's names traded in enough volume today to clear the board's liquidity floor of C$25,000 in day volume, so no individual name is reported here. The DoorDash-Instacart deal and the day's moves in the theme fall on the same trading day; nothing in either release connects one to the other.

entries.headline: Teck Resources' profit jumps to $1.59 billion on copper, zinc prices
entries.dek: The gain from $281 million a year earlier comes as a steelworkers' strike cuts output at the company's Highland Valley Copper mine.

brief: Teck Resources reported third-quarter profit attributable to shareholders of $1.59 billion, or $3.24 per diluted share, up from $281 million, or 57 cents per diluted share, a year earlier. Adjusted profit was $1.88 per diluted share against 76 cents adjusted a year earlier. Revenue rose to $4.52 billion from $3.39 billion.

The company attributed the stronger results to higher copper and zinc prices. Separately, about 1,200 United Steelworkers members began a strike at Teck's Highland Valley Copper mine near Logan Lake, B.C., over the weekend. The mine is continuing to operate at reduced capacity, and the company said the impact on production will depend on the duration of the job action.

On the venture boards, the copper theme comprises 55 listed names; 39 traded today, 7 higher and 22 lower, for a median move of -1.20% against -1.47% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Xxix Metal fell 10.34% to $0.13 and Coyote Copper Mines fell 8.33% to $0.33, while Canadian Copper rose 5.77% to $0.55.
body: Teck Resources reported third-quarter profit attributable to shareholders of $1.59 billion, or $3.24 per diluted share, compared with $281 million, or 57 cents per diluted share, in the same quarter of 2025. On an adjusted basis, the company reported $1.88 per diluted share, against 76 cents adjusted a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter rose to $4.52 billion from $3.39 billion a year earlier.

The company attributed the improvement in both revenue and profit to higher prices for copper and zinc, though it did not disclose specific average realized prices for either metal. Teck's shares, which trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol TECK-B, were quoted at $89.22, up 1.27%, as of the article's publication.

Separately, approximately 1,200 members of the United Steelworkers began a strike at Teck's Highland Valley Copper mine, near Logan Lake, British Columbia, over the weekend. The mine is continuing to operate at reduced capacity during the job action. Teck said the impact of the strike on production will depend on how long it lasts, without giving a specific production estimate or timeline for resolution.

On the venture boards, the copper theme comprises 55 listed venture names. Thirty-nine traded today, seven higher and 22 lower, for a median move of -1.20% against a decline of -1.47% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 0.27 percentage points on the day.

Among names that cleared the board's liquidity floor, Xxix Metal Corp, in the theme on its sector label of Copper, fell 10.34% to $0.13; Coyote Copper Mines, whose registered name contains the word copper, fell 8.33% to $0.33; Canadian Copper, also named for the metal, rose 5.77% to $0.55; Copper Giant Resources fell 5.00% to $0.95; and Super Copper rose 4.44% to $0.47.
Teck's results and the day's moves among the venture copper names fall on the same trading day. Nothing in either disclosure connects one to the other.

entries.headline: Aeon Strategies' crypto audit delay pushes its filing to December 31
entries.dek: The CSE-listed company has applied for a management cease-trade order to avoid a broader halt while its auditor works through complex crypto-related holdings.
entries.caption: An empty boardroom table stands ready for a filing deadline running later than planned.

sources.title: AEON STRATEGIES LTD. Provides Update on Anticipated Late Filing of Annual Financial Statements

unverified_claims: The reasons given for the delay — auditor availability and the complexity of auditing crypto-related investments — rest on the company's and its auditor's own account.
The company's statement that it will apply for, and expects to receive, a management cease trade order is a statement of intent, not a granted order.
brief: Aeon Strategies Ltd. (CSE: AEON), formerly Cloud3 Ventures Inc., said its auditor now expects to complete its annual financial statements by December 31, 2026 — later than the December 4 deadline the company had previously flagged. Davidson & Company LLP cited limited availability and the added time needed for the company's crypto-related investments.

To avoid a general trading halt, Aeon has applied for a management cease trade order, which would bar its CEO and CFO from trading the company's shares until the filings are complete — rather than freezing trading for all shareholders. If regulators do not grant it, a general cease trade order covering all trading remains possible.

Until the annual filings are submitted, Aeon must issue a default status report every two weeks, under National Policy 12-203. The company's auditor is reviewing financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026.
body: Aeon Strategies Ltd. (CSE: AEON, OTCQB: CLDVF, FSE: WQ40), formerly known as Cloud3 Ventures Inc., has updated its timeline for filing annual financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026. The company now expects to file its audited annual filings, management's discussion and analysis and the related CEO and CFO certifications on or before December 31, 2026 — nearly a month later than the December 4, 2026 date it had previously disclosed.

The company's auditor, Davidson & Company LLP, told Aeon that the delay is due to two factors: limited availability on the auditor's side, and the additional time required to complete audit procedures relating to the company's crypto-related investments, which the release says are more complex to audit than in prior years.

To manage the consequences of the late filing, Aeon has applied to its principal regulator for a management cease trade order. If granted, an MCTO would prohibit only the company's chief executive officer and chief financial officer from trading in Aeon's securities until the annual filings are submitted — leaving ordinary shareholders free to continue trading.

The release states that if the management cease trade order is not granted, securities regulators may instead issue a general cease trade order prohibiting all trading in Aeon's securities, a broader measure that would affect every shareholder rather than only its two senior officers.

Until the annual filings are complete, Aeon is required to issue a default status report every two weeks by news release, under the continuous disclosure provisions of National Policy 12-203 covering defaulting reporting issuers.

For investors, the distinction matters: an MCTO limits only who can trade, not whether the stock keeps trading at all, while a general cease trade order would stop every shareholder from buying or selling until the annual filings catch up. Aeon's application for the narrower order is still pending regulatory approval.

entries.headline: Steadright's insiders are expected to buy most of the second tranche
entries.dek: Insiders already took 1,100,000 units of Steadright's first tranche at $0.10, and the company expects them to take most of the rest.
entries.caption: Mineral exploration in arid, mountainous terrain often requires extended logistics and permitting timelines.

sources.title: Steadright Closes First Tranche Of Financing

unverified_claims: The company's expectation that insiders will subscribe for most or all of the remaining units in the second tranche rests on the company's own statement.
The description of Steadright's Moroccan projects (TitanBeach Titanium Project, Copper Valley Project and the Goundafa Mine MOU) rests on the company's own release boilerplate.
brief: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (CSE: SCM), which explores for critical minerals in Morocco, has closed the first tranche of a non-brokered private placement, raising $530,000 at $0.10 per unit. Company insiders subscribed for 1,100,000 of the units in this tranche, at the same price.

Each unit is one common share and one warrant, exercisable at $0.16 per share for 24 months. The securities carry a four-month-and-one-day hold period. The private placement has been upsized by $100,000 to a total of $900,000, with the second and final tranche expected to close within the week.

The company said it expects insiders to subscribe for most or all of the remaining units in the second tranche. Steadright paid finder's fees of $18,600 on 3,100,000 of the units, plus a finder's warrant equal to 6% of gross proceeds, and the offering remains subject to CSE approval.
body: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (CSE: SCM) has closed the first tranche of a non-brokered private placement, raising $530,000 at a price of $0.10 per unit. The closing is the first of two tranches in an offering the company has now upsized to a total of $900,000.

Company insiders subscribed for 1,100,000 of the units sold in this first tranche, at the same $0.10 price offered to other subscribers. The company said it expects insiders to take up most or all of the units remaining in the second and final tranche, which it expects to close within the next week.

Each unit sold in the placement consists of one common share and one common share purchase warrant. Each whole warrant entitles its holder to purchase one additional common share at $0.16 for a period of twenty-four months from closing.

The securities issued in the first tranche are subject to a hold period of four months and one day. The private placement overall was upsized by $100,000 to its current $900,000 total, up to 9,000,000 units in aggregate across both tranches.

Steadright paid finder's fees of $18,600 on 3,100,000 of the units sold in the first tranche, along with a finder's fee warrant equal to 6% of the gross proceeds. The release does not name the recipient, referring only to "eligible parties" under applicable securities laws.

The company describes itself as a mineral exploration business focused on Morocco's critical mineral space, where it holds exposure through a Moroccan entity, NSM Capital Sarl, to more than 192 square kilometres of claims covering the TitanBeach Titanium Project and the Copper Valley Project, plus a binding memorandum of understanding for the historic Goundafa Mine. Proceeds from the placement are earmarked for general working capital, corporate purposes and potential strategic initiatives, and the offering remains subject to approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange.
